semantic_correction.stem: A nurse teaches a parent about physical-activity recommendations for a child age 6 to 17 years. Which guidance is accurate?

options.A: Aim for about 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity each week, adding strengthening mainly for organized sports.
options.B: Use the adult target of about 150 minutes each week because school-age children do not have a separate daily recommendation.
options.C: Get 60 minutes or more daily, mostly aerobic, and include vigorous, muscle-, and bone-strengthening activity at least 3 days weekly.
options.D: Keep activity mostly light intensity and postpone vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening exercise until late adolescence.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC guidance states that children and adolescents ages 6 to 17 need 60 minutes or more of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity every day. Most of the daily activity should be aerobic. Vigorous-intensity aerobic activity, muscle-strengthening activity, and bone-strengthening activity should each be included on at least 3 days per week. Activities should also be age-appropriate, enjoyable, and varied. Therefore option C is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach the current CDC physical-activity recommendation for children and adolescents ages 6 to 17: at least 60 minutes daily with aerobic, vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening components.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened the uniquely long correct answer, preserved all current CDC activity components, and balanced distractors around weekly-vs-daily targets, adult-target substitution, and inappropriate avoidance of strengthening activity.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Child Activity: An Overview — ages 6–17 recommendations
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — physical-activity teaching
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests the current youth activity guideline without a uniquely long keyed response.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. The 60-minute target is daily, not weekly, and strengthening is part of routine youth guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Children ages 6–17 have a distinct daily recommendation rather than the adult weekly target.
option_audit.C: Correct. It matches the CDC daily amount and weekly aerobic/strengthening composition.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activities are recommended during childhood and adolescence.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. C alone includes both the correct daily duration and the recommended activity types/frequency.
cueing_check: All four options are youth physical-activity recommendations of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies C.
